title: Difficulty of first cross and sterility of hybrids correspond only loosely

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Difficulty of first cross and sterility of hybrids correspond only loosely

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Species that are hard to cross generally produce very sterile hybrids, but the correspondence between the difficulty of a first cross and the sterility of the resulting hybrids is by no means strict.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Hybrids from two species which are very difficult to cross, and which rarely produce any offspring, are generally very sterile; but the parallelism between the difficulty of making a first cross, and the sterility of the hybrids thus produced—two classes of facts which are generally confounded together—is by no means strict.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter VIII, “Hybridism”; section “Laws governing the sterility of hybrids”. Scope: interspecific crosses in plants and animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch08-05: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.73

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The proposed correlation is direct and statistically simple. Public data can resolve it within studied groups, but broad paired coverage is incomplete and biased.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For species pairs with both measurements, correlate first-cross success with fertility of their F1 offspring and quantify residual variation. A positive but far-from-perfect association supports the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Paired measurements are scattered.

Successful-cross ascertainment biases estimates of hybrid sterility.

fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.94

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Where both variables were scored on the same pairs, the loose-correspondence claim is a straightforward correlation with a clear null of either a strict line or no association. That test is feasible now for flies and is discriminating within that genus. It remains a restricted-scope test of a claim stated for plants and animals, because comparable paired tables elsewhere are not in one open file.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Correlate an index of how hard a first cross is to make with the sterility of the resulting hybrids, across species pairs. A positive but noisy association, with many pairs off the line, supports a loose correspondence; a tight relationship or no relationship would refute the stated pattern.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Premating scores are an imperfect stand-in for Darwin's 'difficulty of making a first cross'.

Ascertainment favors pairs that someone managed to cross.

The open numerical compilation is essentially Drosophila.
